user_input: Write me a bash script to download a list of multiple files from a website.
model_output:
Here's a bash script that will download multiple files from a website using the `wget` command:
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# set the URL of the website to download from
url="https://example.com/files"

# specify the files to download, one per line
files=(file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt)

# loop through each file and download it
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  # download the file using wget
  wget --recursive --no-clobber --page-requisites --html-extension --convert-links --restrict-file-names=windows --domains website.org --no-parent "$url/$file"
done
```
Here's how the script works:

1. The first line `#!/bin/bash` specifies the interpreter to use to run the script.
2. The `url` variable is set to the URL of the website to download from.
3. The `files` variable is set to an array of files to download, one per line.
4. The `for` loop goes through each file in the `files` array and uses the `wget` command to download it. The `--recursive` option tells `wget` to download all linked files, the `--no-clobber` option prevents overwriting existing files, the `--page-requisites` option downloads all resources needed to display the page, the `--html-extension` option allows for downloading HTML files, the `--convert-links` option converts links to point to the local copies of the downloaded files, the `--restrict-file-names=windows` option restricts file names to Windows format, and the `--domains website.org` option only follows links within the website.org domain.
5. The `--no-parent` option tells `wget` not to go up to the parent directory when downloading files.

Note that this script assumes that the files you want to download are linked from the main page of the website. If the files are linked from other pages on the website, you may need to modify the URL in the `wget` command accordingly.
